quests.title: Teeth in the Meadow
quests.text: Fresh off the south road, and still standing. Good. The wolves have come down out of the woods into the river meadow east of town, and they snap at anyone slower than they are. Thin out 5 Forest Wolves there, {playerName}, then come back and show me the Vale still has teeth of its own.
quests.completion: Five fewer wolves, and you came back walking. That is a fine start. Brother Aldric keeps the chapel just up the road, and he likes to know every new face in Eastbrook. Go and let him put a name to yours.

quests.title: An Arrival Without a Ticket
quests.text: You're breathing, which puts you ahead of your luggage. Gather anything dry from that wreckage while I fetch a blanket. We can discuss your unusual choice of landing place once your teeth stop chattering.
quests.completion: There's bread in that bundle and a blanket without too many holes. Sit a moment, then we'll work out what brought your boat onto the rocks.

quests.title: The Beacon That Lied
quests.text: That beacon should have guided your boat clear of the rocks, not invited it onto them. Someone's been up there, and the rats along the path have started biting anything with a shadow. Have a look inside the lantern, but don't touch anything still burning.
quests.completion: That cord is cold enough to numb my fingers, yet the lantern was lit. I'll wrap it up for Eastbrook's priest, because I prefer my mysteries somewhere other than aboard my boat.

quests.title: The Fish Must Be Consulted
quests.text: Before we discuss fishing, you should understand that the fish consider themselves the injured party. Borrow my spare rod and catch a few minnows for the keep-net. Gently, please, because we're studying them rather than inviting them to supper.
quests.completion: Four healthy minnows, and not one signed complaint. We'll release them after I've checked their scales, which is more courtesy than they showed my last sandwich.

objectives.label: Loan Fishing Rod from the tackle rack
Shore Minnow caught at the jetty

quests.title: Every Board Counts
quests.text: The cargo walkway has developed an interest in dropping people into the sea. Bring me four sound pine logs from the marked trees behind the hut. Leave the old nesting tree alone, unless you'd like to negotiate with thirty furious gulls.
quests.completion: Those will do nicely, and the gulls appear to have spared you. Now we can turn this pile into something people may confidently stand upon.

objectives.label: Shore Pine Logs placed on the timber rack

quests.title: Something Solid Underfoot
quests.text: You've provided the wood, so now comes the business of convincing it to become a walkway. Use my bench and the nails in that chest. I've marked the gaps, although the sea showing through them is also a useful clue.
quests.completion: That feels solid enough for a loaded handcart. It's a small repair, but someone will get home dry because you bothered.

objectives.label: Walkway Panels built at the ferry workbench

quests.title: An Admiral Among Crabs
quests.text: A crab has stolen my hat and now refuses to recognize my authority. Bait the pot beneath the jetty and retrieve it without hurting the little scoundrel. I want my hat back, not a diplomatic incident.
quests.completion: That is my hat, though the crab has improved its ventilation. Let him out once you are finished, because he has already suffered the indignity of being caught by breakfast.

objectives.label: Crab Pot baited with a Bait Herring

quests.title: Across Before the Kettle Boils
quests.text: Eastbrook lies upriver, where people generally arrive through doors rather than shipwrecks. Take this wrapped cord to Brother Aldric at the chapel. Tell him I want an explanation, preferably one that doesn't involve buying a new ferry.
quests.completion: Welcome to Eastbrook, and thank you for bringing this safely. Jorren will find you a warm meal while I examine the cord, but I would like you to return afterward.

quests.title: Someone to Vouch for You
quests.text: A stranger needn't remain one for long here. Take a sample to Ivara, introduce yourself to Corren and Silven, and look at the work posted outside the inn. Eastbrook has room for another pair of willing hands.
quests.completion: Then you have somewhere to begin, and people who know your name. Ivara has already sent word that the thread troubles her, though she cannot yet say why.

objectives.label: Beacon Thread Sample delivered to Ivara

quests.title: Buckles Before Glory
quests.text: The watch wants new breastplates, but half their existing straps won't hold a buckle. Bring me copper and smelt it cleanly. We can discuss glorious weapons after everyone can keep their armor on.
quests.completion: That's clean metal, and I can work with it. A buckle won't earn a ballad, but it might keep the person wearing it alive.

objectives.label: Copper Ore mined in the eastern quarry
Copper Ingot smelted at the public furnace

quests.title: Handle With Considerable Doubt
quests.text: Two labels were exchanged in a minor outbreak of administrative enthusiasm. Ivara needs her mortar, and Brunna needs her padded gloves. Please correct matters before either discovers an exciting new use for the other's order.
quests.completion: Both deliveries are accounted for, and neither customer has demanded my head. That is what I call a successful trading day.

quests.title: The Cold End of the Garden
quests.text: The south bed grows turnips, while the north bed appears to be growing disappointment. Its soil is cold enough to keep butter, even at noon. Bring me good vegetables and a few bad roots before the whole patch decides it's winter.
quests.completion: At least we'll have something for supper. That cord around the fence stake wasn't there when I planted, and I'd like to know who put it there.

quests.title: Nothing Good Tied to a Root
quests.text: I've dug down beside that stake, and someone has tied knots around my roots. Knots, in a vegetable garden, as though the turnips might escape. Take the bindings to Ivara, along with balm for the plants we've had to disturb.
quests.completion: The wax draws warmth from whatever touches it, which explains Della's damaged crop. Removing it should help the bed recover, but please tell her to report anyone digging near her fence.

quests.title: Flowers Facing Down
quests.text: Bertram found the flowers on three graves pushed into the soil, blossoms first. That is not one of our customs, nor a child's joke I recognize. Ask him what he saw and examine the graves without disturbing their occupants.
quests.completion: He heard someone counting after midnight, and this cloth matches the thread Fenlow sent. I would rather have found a thoughtless vandal than someone so careful.

quests.title: The Man Buried on Tuesday
quests.text: Bertram saw a man walking whom we buried together on Tuesday. I have checked the grave, and I fear there is no gentle explanation. Put the Gravestirred to rest and restore their name stones, because whatever moves them now must not take their names as well.
quests.completion: Thank you for treating them as people rather than obstacles. This lamp was never part of their burial, and I will find out who placed it there.

quests.title: The Warmth Gone Missing
quests.text: The roots beside the burial ground have blackened, and even the foxes there have turned savage. Ivara believes the damage may tell us more than the graves alone. Take her herbs from the cold patches and anything tied among the roots.
quests.completion: The soil has been drained of warmth, not poisoned. These bindings match the beacon thread, which means the trouble has been carried here by someone with hands.

quests.title: Please Do Not Pick the Choir
quests.text: Those flowers beneath the bridge have been singing since dawn, and even a happy song becomes tiresome by the seventeenth verse. Lay a damp cloth over each patch before taking a leaf. You needn't pluck the whole choir to borrow a little music.
quests.completion: These leaves still carry a lovely little hum. I'll use them gently, and perhaps the bridge will enjoy a quiet afternoon.

quests.title: Della Takes the Long Way
quests.text: Della took her handcart over the willow path after I warned her about the washout. I've found a wheel, but she shouted back when I called, so there's hope. Bring her and those seed sacks home before she attempts to repair the river.
quests.completion: She came back arguing, which is usually a good sign. Thank you for taking the sacks as well, because she would have gone straight back for them.

quests.title: Three Knocks for Supper
quests.text: Something in my pantry knocks three times whenever I serve supper. The guests say it's a ghost, but ghosts have never previously shown such an interest in dumplings. Find the cause before somebody starts selling tickets.
quests.completion: Those flour prints are smaller than a mouse's, and something has eaten the word 'rent.' Whatever lives in that wall has already understood the expensive part of lodging.

quests.title: A Guest Between the Shelves
quests.text: My pantry key has vanished, and the knocking has become rather impatient. Ask Olvessa what leaves tiny flour prints, then offer our visitor something from the kitchen. I'd prefer a negotiated settlement to dismantling my inn.
quests.completion: A cupboard spirit was tapping through the old speaking pipe to ask for food. It returned my key and offered three buttons for its room, so I believe we're making progress.

objectives.label: Asked Olvessa about the flour prints
Bread set on the Pantry Saucer

quests.title: The Order Nobody Signed
quests.text: Someone needed wax, cord, and lamps for these workings, and those things pass through ordinary hands before reaching wicked ones. Silven may recognize the supplies. Ask what he sold, not what he believes, and let the records answer.
quests.completion: Three buyers used three different names, but all their orders went on the same cart. The destination was Old Kiln Lane, and I dislike being made useful without knowing to whom.

quests.title: Where the Watch Cannot See
quests.text: Neris has found where the supply cart left the road. Go with her while she follows the tracks, and watch the hedges when her eyes are on the ground. We need to know who is there before anyone attempts heroics.
quests.completion: There are people below us tending lamps around an open pit, and something in that pit keeps trying to stand. I'll send word to Aldric while you keep those veils.

quests.title: A Place for What You Keep
quests.text: You keep bringing useful things back to town, and pockets have limits. Build yourself a chest while you consider where you'd like to live. You needn't own a house to begin making a home.
quests.completion: That chest is yours, including everything you eventually manage to squeeze into it. Keep it safe until you've chosen a place, and don't let Silven convince you that hinges count as luxury fittings.

objectives.label: Vale Oak felled in the western coppice
Storage Chest built at Wenna's workbench

quests.title: Room for a Working Life
quests.text: A home ought to hold something you made, and somewhere to make the next thing. Build a worktable, then try arranging it in my demonstration cottage. No purchase required, and please resist testing the walls with an axe.
quests.completion: There you are, with room to work and enough floor left to walk across. Keep the table alongside your chest, because a useful home can begin with very little.

objectives.label: Vale Oak felled in the western coppice
Worktable tried on the Furnishing Practice Marker

quests.title: The Sandwich Emergency
quests.text: The patrol lunches have been stolen twice, and I will not have hungry recruits making decisions with spears. Clear the boars from the shelter and recover the baskets. For the record, I have withdrawn my earlier accusation of organized sabotage.
quests.completion: The watch will eat, and I shall amend my report to say 'persistent livestock.' Nobody needs to know how long I spent questioning the baker.

quests.title: Someone Has Been Teaching Them
quests.text: Neris saw the dead rise when those lamps were lit and collapse when one went out. The people tending them attacked our messenger, so there can be no mistaking their intent. Stop the workings and bring back any instructions you find, because someone taught them this.
quests.completion: The pit is quiet, and those remains can finally be buried properly. These instructions look copied rather than composed, which means the people you stopped may not be the ones who began this.

quests.title: The Promise Under the Paint
quests.text: This copied verse resembles a promise recorded in the Age of First Hearths, though someone has twisted its meaning. Fetch the old prayer boards from the loft and examine the map behind the painted panel. Our founders may have left us a warning worth hearing.
quests.completion: The original promise forbids keeping the dead in service to a crown, while this copy demands their obedience. An old cautionary verse calls such a ruler the Oathless King. The map places the promised resting ground beneath the Hollow Crypt.

objectives.label: Verse compared at the reading desk

quests.title: Supper, Despite Everything
quests.text: Everyone's been working late and pretending they aren't hungry. Help me make a few proper meals, then take them to the people too stubborn to stop. Terrible news can wait while somebody eats a carrot.
quests.completion: Good, because they'll look after the rest of us better with something warm inside them. I've kept a bowl for you, and that wasn't an invitation to argue.

objectives.label: Stew cooked at the inn hearth (2 Brook Trout, 3 Garden Carrots)

quests.title: A Door We Leave Shut
quests.text: The map leads to the Hollow Crypt, but finding a door does not oblige us to open it. Read the boundary stones and give Neris this warning. Stay outside the wicket, whatever you hear beyond it, and come back to me.
quests.completion: Fresh wax beneath the sealed doors is warning enough, and you were right to leave them shut. We will need experienced company before going farther. For tonight, Eastbrook has a watch on the road and one more reason to sleep.

objectives.label: Sealed Watch Warning delivered to Neris

quests.title: Board Bounty: Culvert Rats
quests.text: We've had reports of Culvert Rats troubling people at the town drainage ditch. Remove 5 of them and check your footing while you're there. I don't want a rescue operation attached to a routine patrol.
quests.completion: That should make the route safer for ordinary traffic. Good work, and thank you for returning without requiring a stretcher.

quests.title: Clear Space for Honest Work
quests.text: The workers at the eastern quarry need their hands for tools, not for beating off Quarry Burrowers. Clear 4 from the worksite. I'll pay for a safe shift rather than another tale about why the ore hasn't arrived.
quests.completion: Then we can get something useful made today. You've earned your pay without needing to swing a hammer.

quests.title: Teeth Along the Verge
quests.text: I've marked where Briarbitten Foxes are approaching the road at the northern root hedge. Deal with 4, but leave the healthy wildlife alone. We're protecting a path, not emptying the countryside.
quests.completion: I'll check the verge again on my next round. For now, the travelers behind you have a safer walk.

quests.title: Metal for the Morning Shift
quests.text: I need 6 pieces of Copper Ore from the eastern quarry. Bring sound ore rather than a sack of interesting gravel. The furnace has enough opinions without being fed rubbish.
quests.completion: That's a proper load, and the forge can use all of it. Come back another day when you need honest work.

objectives.label: Copper Ore gathered at the eastern quarry

quests.title: Wood That Has a Future
quests.text: I've orders waiting for 4 Riverside Alder Logs, and the managed brook grove has trees marked for cutting. Leave the unmarked ones standing. Good carpentry begins before the wood reaches the bench.
quests.completion: These will become something useful instead of remaining a sketch on my wall. I'll put the offcuts aside as well, because waste makes expensive furniture.

objectives.label: Alder felled in the brook grove

quests.title: Wood That Has a Future
quests.text: I've orders waiting for 4 Vale Oak Logs, and the western coppice has trees marked for cutting. Leave the unmarked ones standing. Good carpentry begins before the wood reaches the bench.
quests.completion: These will become something useful instead of remaining a sketch on my wall. I'll put the offcuts aside as well, because waste makes expensive furniture.

objectives.label: Vale Oak felled in the western coppice

quests.title: Fresh Leaves, Clean Hands
quests.text: I need 3 fresh Silvermint Sprigs from the eastern meadow. Take the healthy growth and leave enough for each plant to recover. A treatment gathered carelessly begins with an injury of its own.
quests.completion: These are exactly what I needed. Thank you for bringing them promptly rather than letting them wilt beneath a collection of wolf teeth.

objectives.label: Silvermint gathered in the eastern meadow

quests.title: A Receipt Is a Beautiful Thing
quests.text: Please take 3 Hinge Bundles to Wenna at the carpenter's yard. The goods are paid for, properly labeled, and not yours to inspect for personal inspiration. Bring confirmation back, and we shall both enjoy the rare pleasure of an uncomplicated transaction.
quests.completion: Everything is signed for, so everybody knows whom to blame if it goes missing later. Your payment, happily, is considerably less complicated.

quests.title: A Receipt Is a Beautiful Thing
quests.text: Please take 3 Rivet Packets to Brunna at the forge. The goods are paid for, properly labeled, and not yours to inspect for personal inspiration. Bring confirmation back, and we shall both enjoy the rare pleasure of an uncomplicated transaction.
quests.completion: Everything is signed for, so everybody knows whom to blame if it goes missing later. Your payment, happily, is considerably less complicated.

quests.title: Lunch Before Complaints
quests.text: I've prepared 3 Bread Bundles for Neris. Take them straight to the northern lookout, because hungry people can turn a short delay into a lifelong grievance. Anything you smell along the way remains part of the delivery.
quests.completion: Good, because the kitchen was already receiving complaints from imaginary future customers. There's something small for you on the counter, and this time you're permitted to eat it.

quests.title: Lunch Before Complaints
quests.text: I've prepared 3 Covered Stew Bowls for Corren. Take them straight to the training yard, because hungry people can turn a short delay into a lifelong grievance. Anything you smell along the way remains part of the delivery.
quests.completion: Good, because the kitchen was already receiving complaints from imaginary future customers. There's something small for you on the counter, and this time you're permitted to eat it.

objectives.label: Covered Stew Bowls delivered to Corren

quests.title: Small Parcels, Growing Things
quests.text: I've set aside 3 Dried Herb Packets for Ivara at the apothecary. Carry them gently and keep them dry. Things that grow deserve a little care even when they're wrapped in string.
quests.completion: Then something will be tended that might otherwise have been neglected. Small journeys can do a surprising amount of good.

objectives.label: Dried Herb Packets delivered to Ivara

quests.title: Small Parcels, Growing Things
quests.text: I've set aside 3 Reed Mulch Bundles for Della at the riverside garden. Carry them gently and keep them dry. Things that grow deserve a little care even when they're wrapped in string.
quests.completion: Then something will be tended that might otherwise have been neglected. Small journeys can do a surprising amount of good.

objectives.label: Reed Mulch Bundles delivered to Della

quests.title: A Road Checked Properly
quests.text: Check 3 Quay Inspection Posts along the riverside walk and report what you actually find. Do not substitute what a passing merchant claims his cousin saw. We have an entire council for that.
quests.completion: That's a useful report, with places and observations rather than adjectives. I'll pass it to the next watch before they set out.

quests.title: A Road Checked Properly
quests.text: Check 3 Road Checkposts along the south road and report what you actually find. Do not substitute what a passing merchant claims his cousin saw. We have an entire council for that.
quests.completion: That's a useful report, with places and observations rather than adjectives. I'll pass it to the next watch before they set out.

quests.title: Leave a Light Behind You
quests.text: Several lamps along the Briar Gate circuit are running low. Take oil for 3 Watch Lanterns and check their shutters while you are there. Someone coming home late should be able to see the next safe place.
quests.completion: I'll be able to follow that line of lights on tonight's round. So will everyone else who needs to reach home.

quests.title: The Road, Not the Rumor
quests.text: I've heard three alarming accounts of the town's brook crossings, none from anyone who's visited them today. Inspect 3 Water-Level Gauges and bring me facts. Rumors are remarkably expensive when attached to a delivery schedule.
quests.completion: Excellent, because now I can arrange deliveries around the conditions rather than the gossip. Reliable information is a commodity I am occasionally willing to pay for.

quests.title: Cargo From a Ship That Sank Twice
quests.text: Crates have been washing up on the quay all morning, and they are dry inside. Wood that has been under the sea for years does not stay dry, {playerName}, and neither do I when I think about it too long. Bring me three of them and read the mark stenciled on the one the tide left by the bell.
quests.completion: Gilt Measure seal, an old one, on a ship the harbor rolls say went down twice: once in a storm, and once again when someone tried to raise her. Either the sea is returning things, or someone wants us to think it is.

quests.title: Whose Seal Is This
quests.text: The seal is a Pressford cider consignment, booked, paid and blessed, that never left the press. Carry my ledger copy south across the causeway to the cider-master and read the town's shipping roll. If the cider sailed, someone drank a ghost.
quests.completion: That is my booking, my seal and my signature, for a harvest this town never pressed. I have a cellar full of empty barrels and a head full of a summer I cannot remember. Sit down. I will pour you something that definitely exists.

objectives.label: Ledger copy delivered to Pressford's cider-master

quests.title: Bells You Can Hear From the Steps
quests.text: The fish below the town steps have gone nervous. Not shy, nervous, the way a cat goes nervous before a storm. Catch a few for my kitchen, then hold this old horn to the jetty post and tell me I am imagining the ringing.
quests.completion: You heard it too. Bells, under the water, slow as a funeral. Well. The fish are excellent, and I intend to serve them before they hear anything else.

objectives.label: Skittish Harbor Fish caught off the town steps
Listened at the old jetty post

quests.title: A Lantern for the Causeway
quests.text: The lanterns on the southern causeway keep going out, and a lantern that goes out on a sea road is a trap with good manners. Take this oil off the Farshore's south point, fill the three lamps on the way down, and report to the watch sergeant at the far end.
quests.completion: Three lights where there were none, and you still have your boots. The sea breathed on those lamps all week. We will see whether it likes the taste of fresh oil.

quests.title: Causeway Watch
quests.text: The cold cord from the Proving Shore beacon, the dry cargo, the bells Jorren swears he hears: every thread I pull runs south. Take this bundle of cord to the Causeway Watch and put it in a sergeant's hands. Tell him Eastbrook is listening.
quests.completion: This is the same cord we cut off the waybill thieves last week. So Eastbrook has the head of the snake and we have the tail. I would very much like to meet the middle.

objectives.label: Proving Shore cord handed to the watch

quests.title: The Watch Holds the Road
quests.text: Somebody is paying cutpurses to stop every cart heading inland, and paying them well enough that they have started wearing clean boots. Thin them out near the old press and bring back the waybills they lifted. I want to know whose cargo frightens somebody.
quests.completion: Cider barrels, empty. Cider barrels, empty. Cider barrels, full of nothing anyone can name. Whoever wants this road shut is guarding a harvest that never happened.

quests.title: Pressford Remembers a Harvest
quests.text: Half the town swears we pressed a harvest this summer, and the other half swears we did not, and both halves are carrying the same tally sticks. Knock on three doors, ask what they remember, and collect any tally stick that disagrees with itself.
quests.completion: Every stick counts a barrel, and every barrel is in a cellar that is empty. We remember the work but not the fruit. Someone harvested us, {playerName}, and I would like to know with what kind of basket.

quests.title: Pests in the Windfalls
quests.text: The boars have found the windfalls under Blossom Rise, and they have gone bold about it, which boars should never be. Drive them off and gather the good apples before they finish the hill. Bruised is fine. Bitten is a conversation.
quests.completion: Six good apples, and a hillside that smells of cider instead of pig. The trees have been dropping fruit out of season. I would call it generosity if trees did that sort of thing.

quests.title: The Press Will Not Turn
quests.text: The great press seized overnight. Not rusted, not broken: seized, as if it decided it had pressed enough. Its main gear has split clean through, and oak is the only wood that will take that load. Take my axe, fell the oaks I have marked behind the yard, and cut me a new gear at the town bench. Then fit it, and we shall see who is more stubborn.
quests.completion: Listen to that. Wood on wood, and the whole town leaning out of its windows to hear it. A press is only a gear and a promise, {playerName}, and you have just kept the second one for them.

objectives.label: Oak Press Gear cut at the bench
New gear fitted to the Great Cider Press

quests.title: Cord in the Cider Vat
quests.text: The press turns again, and the first thing it did was choke. Something is wound around the outflow of the old vat, something that was not there when we scrubbed it in spring. Open the drain, fish out whatever it is, and take it to the brother at the Eastbrook chapel. I am a cider-master, not a priest, and this feels like a priest problem.
quests.completion: Black cord, cold enough to ache, knotted the way the beacon on the Proving Shore was knotted. The same hands, {playerName}. Whoever tied the light that lied to the ships has been in Pressford's cellars too, and they were not there for the cider.

quests.title: Seed for a Second Planting
quests.text: Three rows here went grey in a single night. Not dead, mind you, just tired of being trees. Before the frost comes I mean to sow them again. Pick me some hedge sorrel from under Blossom Rise, the roots bind the seed, and I will show you how to make a pouch of it at my bench. Then sow the grey rows, and talk to them nicely while you do.
quests.completion: Look, green already, and they are not even pretending to be slow about it. Some ground only needs to be told it is wanted. I find the same is true of most people, {playerName}, and nearly all gardeners.

objectives.label: Seed pouch made at the field bench

quests.title: The Door We Left Shut
quests.text: We were right to leave the crypt shut. I would like that on record before I say the next part: it has to be opened now. Look at the Outer Wicket for me, then fetch the key from the sexton's lodge. Bring both your eyes and the key to Brother Aldric, in that order of importance.
quests.completion: The wicket's ward has gone cold, and the key is warm. That is backwards in every way that matters. Very well. The crypt opens, and I will pray for whoever goes in first. That will be you.

quests.title: A Kitchen for the Pickers
quests.text: Word from Pressford: the pickers have worked through supper every night this week, and the cider-master is too busy to notice. It could be worse. Usually is. Catch three trout off our own steps, carry them south, pick a few apples from the trees above the orchard, and bake the lot into pies at the cookhouse hearth. Then feed the pickers before they start eating the harvest.
quests.completion: Pies? Jorren sent pies? Then I owe that man a barrel, and the pickers owe you their good temper. They have stopped arguing about who forgot the harvest and started arguing about crusts. That, {playerName}, is a town getting better.

objectives.label: Orchard Pies baked from 3 trout and 3 apples
Orchard Pie handed to a picker

quests.title: Moor Hounds at the Peat Cuts
quests.text: The hounds on this moor have always been a nuisance, but they have never been clever. Now they work the peat cuts in packs and herd the cutters off the ground, the way a dog herds sheep. I want them thinned before somebody is herded into a bog. Bring me some pelts while you are at it: Tanner Hesk in Fenbridge pays well, and the camp needs boots.
quests.completion: Four good pelts and a moor that only growls at a distance. Whatever taught them to herd, it did not teach them to count. That is the first piece of luck Ferncross has had all month, {playerName}.

quests.title: Fires That Should Not Burn
quests.text: There are fires down in the peat cuts that have been burning for three days on nothing. No wood, no peat, no oil. Something small and bright dances around them, and it bites. Take this pail of tarn water, chase off whatever is tending them, and put the fires out. If they will not go out, come back quickly and do not tell the cutters.
quests.completion: Out, all three, and the ground under them was cold. Cold, {playerName}, under a fire. I have stopped pretending this moor is only a moor. Thank you for coming back with both eyebrows.

objectives.label: Fire with nothing to burn doused

quests.title: Bandit Pay
quests.text: The bandits on the Heath Way are paid, and paid well: every one we catch has a purse of new coin, still bright, still stamped. Bandits do not earn new coin. Somebody hands it to them. Take three purses off them and carry them to Silven Brackett in Eastbrook. He knows the Gilt Measure's stamps better than he knows his own mother.
quests.completion: Minted this spring, struck at a Gilt Measure house, and paid out to men who rob carts. I would like to say I am shocked. I am mostly offended, {playerName}: somebody is spending my guild's good name on cutthroats, and I intend to find out who.

quests.title: A Keeper's Escort
quests.text: The circle keepers have walked to the old stones every week for longer than Ferncross has had a name. This week Agnes Tarnby would not go alone, and Agnes has walked that moor through two winters and a wedding. Walk her to the Ring, {playerName}. Keep the hounds off her, and keep her talking: she goes quiet when she is frightened, and the moor goes quiet with her.
quests.completion: Agnes says the stones were warm when she touched them, warm as a hearth with nobody tending it. She also says you are a good listener, which from Agnes is very nearly a knighthood.

objectives.label: Agnes Tarnby escorted to the Ring

quests.title: The First Hearth Ring
quests.text: Brother Aldric sent me this fragment, and it has been warm in my hand all the way across the moor. These stones are older than any kingdom: the folk who raised them lit the first hearths. Touch each stone so they know you, then set the fragment on the hearth stone at the centre. The woods are listening, {playerName}. So are the stones. Be polite.
quests.completion: Did you feel it? The fragment answered the hearth, the way a child answers its name. The Hearthpins were made from fires like this one. Whatever is pulling them apart, it has to pull against something very old.

objectives.label: Hearthpin fragment set on the hearth stone

quests.title: Ash From Before the Kingdom
quests.text: The ash around the hearth stone is not from any fire I know. It is fine as flour and it smells of rain. Gather a few samples, carefully, and take them to Orwin Pellock in Eastbrook. He will forget his lunch, his hat and possibly his name, but he will not forget what this ash means.
quests.completion: This ash is older than the first kingdom. Older than Eastbrook, older than the road, older than the idea of a road. That is either impossible or extremely inconvenient. Where did you say you found it? No, do not tell me yet. Let me be astonished properly first.

quests.title: Heath Herbs for the Fen Healers
quests.text: The fog sickness is spreading faster than my shelves can follow. Heath mallow draws the fever, but it only grows on the open Kindlemoor, off the Heath Way. Pick me six good stems, bring them back to my mixing table here, and grind them into two poultices. I will show you the grind. Mind your thumbs: the mallow does not.
quests.completion: Two poultices, smooth and sharp-smelling, and two fevers broken before supper. You would make a fair apothecary, {playerName}, if you could ever be persuaded to stand still.

objectives.label: Marsh Poultice ground at the mixing table

quests.title: Remembered Roofs
quests.text: Three houses stand along the causeway road this morning. I have walked that road every day for eleven years, and I would have noticed houses. Knock, look inside, and bring me anything left on the sills. Handle it gently; I suspect it remembers more than we do.
quests.completion: A child's shoe, a wedding spoon, a letter to nobody. Each one is wet, and none of them has been near water. Someone is building homes out of what people have forgotten. I will write this down before I forget it as well.

quests.title: A Bridge Fenbridge Can Trust
quests.text: The boardwalk is sinking a hand's width a week, and the fog is not helping. Take my hatchet, fell the alders I have marked, and turn them into planks at the bench. Then replace the two spans that have started making noises a bridge should not make.
quests.completion: Solid as a promise, and quieter than most. Fenbridge walks dry tonight because you spent your afternoon on planks instead of glory. I will not forget it, which these days is saying something.

objectives.label: Boardwalk Planks cut at the bench

quests.title: Paddy Work in the Fog
quests.text: There is a harvest standing in my west paddy, and I do not remember sowing it. My hands do, apparently. Bundle what is ripe along the causeway bank, and empty my two eel traps before the eels eat the rest.
quests.completion: Good rice, fat eels, and not one memory of planting either. I have decided to be grateful rather than frightened. It is easier on the knees.

objectives.label: Paddy Eel taken from the traps

quests.title: Coin for a Quiet Road
quests.text: I have found where the bright coin goes. Coinwell Camp, out on the Chalkbarrow Coast, pays a 'road fee' every month, and that fee buys exactly the bandits the Causeway Watch keeps fighting. Carry this sealed payment to their claim-master and look at his claim posts while you are there. I want to see his face, and I want you to see his posts.
quests.completion: This is Silven's seal, and that is my fee, and those are my posts, and not one of them marks the claim I paid for. Somebody has been taking my money to keep a road quiet that I never asked to have quiet. Sit down, {playerName}. I need to be angry at someone who is not you.

objectives.label: Sealed payment handed to the claim-master

quests.title: The Claim Nobody Filed
quests.text: Somebody is filing claims on this coast, in my hand, under my seal, on land that is not there yet. Not sold, not surveyed: not there. The papers travel in the wagons on the coast road. Bring me three of them, and do not read them aloud. I have a superstition about land that does not exist, and I would like to keep it.
quests.completion: Low-water lines, {playerName}. Every claim is drawn on ground that only shows when the tide goes out further than it ever has. Somebody expects the sea to step back, and means to own what it leaves.

quests.title: Ore With a Will
quests.text: The prospectors bring me ore from the veins short of the Dig, and it is warm in the hand. Ore is not warm. Ore is honest and cold and does what it is told. Take my assay pick, cut a good load from the veins I marked, and smelt it into one test ingot at the camp forge. Then we will see what it has to say for itself.
quests.completion: Feel it. It holds heat like a hearthstone and leans toward the sea when you set it down. Metal tells the truth, {playerName}, and this metal says it would very much like to be a bell. I do not intend to let it.

objectives.label: Kindle Ore cut from a marked vein
Kindle Test Ingot smelted at the camp forge

quests.title: Lanterns That Will Not Light
quests.text: The Unlit Dig was a Coinwell claim until the veiled diggers walked in and took it. No flame stays lit at its mouth: not a candle, not a forge, not a pipe. Take this taper, it was lit at the camp hearth and it is stubborn, and light the four lamps at the mouth. Kill whatever crawls out while you work. I want light on that hole before I want anything else.
quests.completion: Four lamps, still burning, and the crawlers backing off from them like the light is hot to the touch. The Lanternwardens have a saying about that, I am told. I never listened. I am listening now, {playerName}.

quests.title: What the Dig Was For
quests.text: With the lamps lit we can see inside the Dig, and I do not like what we can see. The veiled diggers are not mining. They are casting. Go in, {playerName}, put ten of them down, and bring me whatever they are casting from. I need to know what is worth this much warm ore, this much stolen coin and this many lies.
quests.completion: A clapper. A bell clapper, cast from ore that wants to be a bell. Somebody is giving the drowned bells new tongues, and every one they hang rings the tide a little further out. The cord, the coin, the claims: it is all one plan, and the plan is to drown the harbor.

quests.title: Chalk Cliff Nests
quests.text: The gulls off the White Head have been lining their nests with buttons. Brass buttons. Coat buttons, the sort sailors wear, and no sailor has stood on that cliff in years. I would like the gulls to stop, and I would like the buttons back, and I would like somebody else to climb up there. That somebody is you, {playerName}.
quests.completion: Every one of these is stamped with a ship and a harbor. Drowned men's buttons, brought up out of the sea. Gulls steal from the living all the time. When they start stealing from the drowned, it means the sea is giving things back. I will light a candle tonight.

quests.title: Bells at Low Tide
quests.text: I have sailed this coast for thirty years, {playerName}, and the tide has never once lied to me. It is lying now. The water goes out too far and comes in too fast, and every time it turns, I hear bells. Strike the three gauges on the White Head shore at low water, and catch me a few of the fish that float up stunned after the ringing. I need proof before the next flood.
quests.completion: The gauges dropped a hand past any mark I have ever cut, and the fish are struck dumb, every one, as if a great bell rang beside them. The bells are pulling the tide. When they pull hard enough to let go, Eastbrook harbor drowns.

objectives.label: Tide gauge struck at low water
Bell-Struck Fish caught off the White Head

quests.title: A Tide Road to the Fortress
quests.text: There is a road under the sea. The old builders laid it from Wreckers' Cove to the drowned fortress, and at the lowest tide its first stones show. It needs braces before anyone sets foot on it. Take my chisel, cut chalk blocks from the faces under the White Head, shape two braces at the camp bench, and set them on the footings in the cove. Measure twice. The sea will not let you measure a third time.
quests.completion: They hold. I stood on the first brace and the sea pushed at it and the brace pushed back. Somebody built this road a very long time ago because they meant to come home along it, {playerName}. Now somebody can.

objectives.label: Chalk Block cut from the cliff face
Tide-Road Brace shaped at the camp bench
Tide-road brace set on its footing

quests.title: Strongboxes on the Shoals
quests.text: That ship that sank twice: her strongboxes are washing up in Wreckers' Cove on the Chalkbarrow Coast, sealed with Gilt Measure wax. Our own wax, {playerName}, on a cargo we never insured. The Gilt Measure would like its lost goods back, and I would like to know who has been sealing things in our name. Bring me four boxes, unopened. I mean that. Unopened.
quests.completion: Unopened, as promised. You are a credit to honest commerce, which is a small club. Inside are ledgers, and the ledgers are paid in memories: so much a summer, so much a wedding. I think I am going to need a stronger drink than this.

quests.title: Silk in the Heather
quests.text: Widows have spun over the heather east of the cuts, and my cutters walk into the webs every morning with a spade in one hand and a scream in the other. Clear them out for me. And bring back some of that silk: wound tight, it makes the best drying lines on the moor.
quests.completion: Five good hanks and a heath you can walk across without dancing. The cutters will sing about you, {playerName}. Badly, but they will sing.

quests.title: The Barrow Walkers
quests.text: South of the Hearth Ring the old barrows have started to empty, and what climbs out walks the moor at dusk. They do not want our peat and they do not want our coin. They just walk, and anything in their way gets walked over. Lay them back down, {playerName}, gently if you can and firmly if you cannot.
quests.completion: Quiet again, and the barrows only barrows. Tamsin says the moor is listening to something. I say it is listening to you now.

quests.title: Peat for the Cutters
quests.text: The hounds have kept my cutters off the drying stacks for a week, and wet peat does not burn. Go down to the cuts and bring me a brick from each stack while the weather holds. The hounds will not thank you. Neither will your back.
quests.completion: Dry as a sermon, every brick. Ferncross will be warm tonight, and that is your doing.

objectives.label: Peat brick taken from a stack

quests.title: Prowlers on the Heath
quests.text: Prowlers have come up from the south heath and taken two of our ponies. A pony is a cart, and a cart is how the peat gets to market. Thin them out before they get bold enough to try the camp.
quests.completion: No more tracks by the pony line this morning. The carts roll again. Thank you, {playerName}.

quests.title: Word to Panwick
quests.text: Panwick buys half my peat to boil their brine, and the Pan-Reeve has not sent a cart in a fortnight. Odda Brinewell does not miss a fortnight. Take the Applewold road south over the Saltmeads gate and find out what is keeping her. If it is trouble, she will be glad of you. If it is not, buy me some salt.
quests.completion: Wat sent you? Then he has worked out something is wrong before I have had time to write it down. Sit. There is more trouble in Panwick than there are pans, and I have a great many pans.

objectives.label: Speak with Odda Brinewell in Panwick

quests.title: Claws in the Pans
quests.text: Scuttlers. Up out of the shallows and into the settling pans, snipping at anyone who bends over the brine. A boiler with no fingers is a boiler with no job. Go and teach them the pans are ours.
quests.completion: Ten fewer claws and I can finally rake a pan without counting my fingers after. You have the makings of a salter, {playerName}.

quests.title: Stolen Salt
quests.text: Looters have been carrying off whole sacks from the drying sheds by night and camping west of the pans as if they owned the place. Salt is the only coin this town has. Get my sacks back, and if the looters object, let them object to you.
quests.completion: Six sacks, still dry. You would not believe how hard it is to find someone who can carry salt through a fight without spilling it.

quests.title: Skimming the Pans
quests.text: Now the scuttlers are gone, the pans need skimming before the brine sours. Go out to the Brine Pans and take a skim from each pan rim. Keep the scum out of it. If it is grey, it is wrong. If it is pink, run.
quests.completion: Clean, clear and sharp as a winter morning. Those will boil down into the best salt Panwick has made all season.

quests.title: Fleece for the Salters
quests.text: Salters work with their hands in brine all day, and brine eats skin. The rams on the salt downs grow a fleece so greasy the brine slides right off it. Bring me some and the whole crew will have gloves by winter.
quests.completion: Greasy, thick and smelling of the downs. The crew will grumble about the smell for a week and then never take the gloves off.

quests.title: What the Tide Brought
quests.text: The tide has started bringing in more than salt. Drowned men walk up out of the shallows east of the pans, still in salter aprons, still carrying rakes. Some of them I knew. Put them to rest, {playerName}. I cannot ask the town to do it.
quests.completion: Thank you. I will have their names read in the square tonight, the ones I can still remember. Something sent them back to us. I want to know what.

quests.title: A Ledger in the Brine
quests.text: Every salter carries a tally book in a waxed pouch, and the drowned still wear theirs. One of them will say where they were working when the water took them. Find me a ledger that can still be read.
quests.completion: Waterlogged, but legible. The last page is a tally of salt sold to a buyer with no name, paid in new coin, delivered to the Wychwold road. Salt does not go west, {playerName}. Nobody in the wold needs that much.

quests.title: Bloats on the Saltings
quests.text: Bloats have drifted onto the saltings east of town and they sour every pan they float near. Pop them, from a distance if you have any sense. I will not be helping with the washing afterwards.
quests.completion: I could smell that from here. The pans will forgive you. Your boots may not.

quests.title: The Salt Cart
quests.text: Nan Saltash takes the cart out to the Brine Pans for the morning skim, and twice this week the scuttlers have come up out of the water for her. Walk with her to the pans. If that ledger is right, I will need every sack we can make before somebody else comes asking for it.
quests.completion: Nan says you kept the scuttlers off the cart and only lost your temper once. From Nan, that is high praise.

objectives.label: Nan Saltash escorted to the Brine Pans

quests.title: The Salt Way West
quests.text: The ledger says the salt went west along the salt way, into the Wychwold. The Bracken Circle keeps a lodge at Elmhallow and Hesper Elmsley knows every cart that has rolled through the wold in thirty years. Take her the news, and ask her who in the wold is buying salt by the cartload.
quests.completion: Salt by the cartload? Out here? Nobody in the wold salts anything but the odd ham. Then somebody is buying it for something else, and I do not like the list of things that need that much salt.

objectives.label: Speak with Hesper Elmsley at Elmhallow

quests.title: Wolves at the Clamps
quests.text: A clamp has to be watched day and night or it burns through and you are left with ash. The wolves know it. They wait until a burner dozes and then they come for the lunch basket, and sometimes for the burner. Drive them off east of the lodge.
quests.completion: The pack has gone quiet. My lads slept last night for the first time in a week, and only two clamps burned through. That is a good week, {playerName}.

quests.title: Tusks and Tempers
quests.text: The boars north of the lodge root up the turf we stack over the clamps, and a clamp with no turf is just a bonfire. Bring me some tusks. The Circle carves them into pegs for the turf, which the boars find very insulting.
quests.completion: Good, sharp tusks. There is a kind of justice in pegging their own turf down with them.

quests.title: Cold Clamps
quests.text: Four of my clamps in the hollow went cold overnight. Not burned out: cold, with the wood still inside, like something drank the fire out of them. Take this firebrand down to the hollow and light them again. If they will not take, come back and tell me, and we will both pretend we are not worried.
quests.completion: They took, all four, though you say the smoke came out the wrong way at first. Into the ground instead of up. I will be asking Hesper about that.

quests.title: Silk in the Elms
quests.text: Weavers have strung the elms south of here so thick that the light does not reach the floor. The Circle does not hurt the wold lightly, but a wood with no light is a dying wood. Cut them back, and bring me their silk. We weave it into the binding cords for the Knotted Elm.
quests.completion: Light on the wold floor again, and enough silk to bind the elm for a year. Thank you. Now I can show you what I have been afraid to look at alone.

quests.title: Under the Roots
quests.text: The old wold folk buried their dead among the roots of the Knotted Elm, so the tree would keep them. Now the tree is letting them go. They climb out of the roots and stand around the trunk as if they are waiting for someone. Lay them down again, {playerName}, before they decide who.
quests.completion: Still now, all of them. They were facing the same way, east, toward the salt way. Whatever the salt is for, the dead under the elm know about it.

quests.title: The Knotted Elm
quests.text: The elmroot dead wear knotted charms, the old binding the wold folk tied before the first hearth. Gather some from them, then go to the Knotted Elm and lay your hand on the trunk. If the binding still holds, you will feel it. If it does not, tell me what you felt instead.
quests.completion: Cold, you say, and pulling toward the south-west. Toward the Tinmarch. Someone is taking salt and fire out of this country and sending it somewhere under the ground. The miners at Wheal Patience will know where the ground has been opened.

quests.title: Tinners' Ford
quests.text: Cross Tinners' Ford into the Tinmarch and find Captain Tobias Penhallow at Wheal Patience. He is a Gilt Measure man and he will want to argue about who pays for what. Let him. Then tell him the elm is pulling toward his moor, and watch his face.
quests.completion: The elm, pulling toward my moor. That is the second strange thing I have heard this week, and the first was a crew of strangers opening the old Blackadit without a licence. Sit down. I think we have the same problem.

objectives.label: Speak with Tobias Penhallow at Wheal Patience

quests.title: Rats in the Spoil
quests.text: Diggers have burrowed into the spoil heaps east of camp, and a spoil heap full of tunnels is a spoil heap waiting to fall on somebody. Clear them out before my insurers hear about it.
quests.completion: The heaps have stopped twitching. My insurers will never know how close they came to paying out. Neither will my wife.

quests.title: Stalkers on the Moor
quests.text: I walk the moor north of camp for samples, and lately something walks behind me. Stalkers, a whole family of them, and they have learned that an assayer with her nose in a rock does not look up. Make them reconsider.
quests.completion: I walked the north moor this morning and nothing followed me but my own shadow. You cannot assay peace of mind, but I would put a high value on it.

quests.title: Stolen Lamps
quests.text: Tunnelers came up from the Blackadit and stripped our lamp store bare. A miner with no lamp is a miner with no work, and the shift is waiting. They are camped by the old working south-east of here. Bring the lamps home.
quests.completion: Six lamps, and every one of them with the Wheal Patience mark scratched off and a pale sigil scratched on. Somebody is supplying those tunnelers, {playerName}. Tunnelers do not draw sigils.

quests.title: Assay Samples
quests.text: The spoil heaps east of camp should be worthless: that is what spoil means. But my lamp flickers when I walk past them. Bring me a sample from each heap. Do not lick them. I am told people need telling.
quests.completion: Tin, mostly. And something else, bright as a struck spark and humming like a kettle. It is not ore. I do not know what it is, and that is not a sentence an assayer likes to say.

objectives.label: Ore sample taken from a spoil heap

quests.title: The Humming Stones
quests.text: The hum in those samples leads to the Stannary Stones, west of camp. Living stone walks there now, tin and quartz grown legs, and it hums the same note. Break a few apart and bring me the cores. Carefully. I want to know what is singing.
quests.completion: Hold one to your ear. That hum is a hearth, {playerName}. A hearth with no fire, pulled up out of the ground and left to walk. Someone is drawing the old fires out of this country, and the stones are what is left over.

quests.title: Who Opened the Blackadit
quests.text: The Blackadit was sealed before my grandfather was born. It floods, it falls in and it eats lamps. Now a crew in pale coats has opened it and set the tunnelers to work for them. They are the Pale Accord, the same crew Coinwell chased off the chalk. Drive them out of my moor.
quests.completion: They fought like people with somewhere to be. Whatever they are digging for, they think it is worth more than tin. That frightens me more than they did.

quests.title: Orders in Pale Ink
quests.text: A crew that organized carries orders. Find them. I want to know who signs for salt from Panwick, firebrands from the wold and the old fires from under my moor, and I want it in their own hand.
quests.completion: Salt to keep the deep workings dry, charcoal to keep them lit, and the hearths under the moor drawn up and sent on in sealed carts. No name at the bottom, only that pale sigil. This is bigger than one mine, {playerName}. I will send copies to Panwick, Elmhallow and the Gilt Measure's own house before the week is out.

quests.title: Shore Up the Blackadit
quests.text: I cannot seal a mine my grandfather could not, but I can make it too much trouble to use. Take these pit props down to the three workings the Accord opened round the Blackadit and brace them shut. Nobody gets through a braced working without a week of work and a great deal of noise, and my lads will be listening.
quests.completion: Three workings braced and my lads posted on the spoil heaps. The Accord will be back, but they will have to knock first. Wheal Patience will not forget it, {playerName}. Neither will I.

quests.title: Barrow Grave-Goods
quests.text: The walkers carry things out of the barrows with them: brooches, combs, little clay hearths no bigger than your thumb. Those belong in the ground with their owners. Bring me what they carry and I will see the keepers put it all back where it was.
quests.completion: Clay hearths, every one of them. The old moor folk buried their dead with a fire to carry. I will have Agnes take them back to the barrows at first light.

quests.title: Amber off the Herd
quests.text: The gilded stags bed down beneath my oldest trees, and the sap drips gold into their coats all night. Combed clots of it are the purest amber in the weald. Bring me six, {playerName}. The stags will not thank you, but they will not miss it either.
quests.completion: Six clots, clean as poured honey. These gloves are stitched with the last batch, {playerName}: sap-stiffened, and warmer than they look.

quests.title: Foxes in the Lamplight
quests.text: The gloam foxes have learned what the lantern stores are worth, {playerName}. Every dusk they slip the fences and carry off the tallow we press for the ferry lamps. Soft paws, softer conscience. Cull ten of them and the rest will remember to fear the town.
quests.completion: Ten, and the stores went untouched last night for the first time this season. The lamplighters send their thanks, {playerName}.

quests.title: The Gold Road Down
quests.text: You came over the Goldmelt, {playerName}, snow still on your boots. I keep this shrine so Lanternmere knows who walks in from the cold, and lately I have had little to report. Take the gold road down to the town, find Reeve Ottoline by the well, and tell her the pass is quiet.
quests.completion: Quiet on the Goldmelt, and a traveler with snow in their hair to prove it. Sorrel keeps her watch too well to send idle word. Be welcome in Lanternmere, {playerName}. The lanterns burn for you.

quests.title: Lanterns on the Water
quests.text: Every ferry on the Mere carries a stern lantern, {playerName}, and three of my boats came back at dawn without theirs. The fog took them, or something in the fog did. They wash up along the east shore when the wind turns. Walk the shore road and bring my lanterns home.
quests.completion: All three, and still burning. Ferry lanterns do not go out in water, {playerName}. That is the point of them. What worries me is what pulled them loose.

quests.title: A Cart for the Orchard
quests.text: Orchardist Pomeline keeps the Gilded Orchard on the west road, and her sap carts are three days overdue. The whole town runs on that amber sap, {playerName}: lamp resin, sweetening, the harvest ale. Walk the west road and find out what keeps her.
quests.completion: The Reeve counts her carts, does she? Well, she can count them missing a while longer. Look at my rows, {playerName}. I have greater troubles than a late delivery.

quests.title: Sprites and Spigots
quests.text: Harvest sprites, {playerName}. They pry my sap-taps from the trunks for the sweetness inside and fling the buckets into the grass. Drive off eight of the little thieves and bring back four of my buckets, and the carts roll again.
quests.completion: Four buckets back on their hooks and the rows gone quiet. You have a heavier hand with sprites than I do, {playerName}, and today I am glad of it.

quests.title: The Meredark
quests.text: The old ferrymen have a name they only say ashore: the Meredark, the first lurker, old as the lake and twice as patient. It rose once before, the year the drowned jetty went under, and it is rising now. At dusk it suns itself on the jetty ruin off the south shore, {playerName}. Take a friend, take two, and end it while it can still be ended.
quests.completion: The fog lifted off the Mere this morning, {playerName}, and the whole town saw it. The ferries will run the night crossing again, and every lantern on the water will burn in your name. Take this: it was dredged from the drowned jetty, and no one has better right to wear it.

quests.title: What Took the Moorings
quests.text: Now I will tell you what I did not say in front of the town. The moorings were not slipped, they were bitten through. Mere lurkers, bolder every night, dragging at the ropes and the rudders. Put eight of them back under the water for good, {playerName}, before a ferryman goes with them.
quests.completion: Eight fewer shapes in the shallows, and the crossing ran on time today for the first time in a fortnight. But bold lurkers are driven lurkers, {playerName}. Something beneath the Mere is moving them.

quests.title: Bandits of the Vale
quests.text: A pack of cutthroats has made camp in the northwest hills. They have robbed three wagons this week. Drive them out: slay 10 Vale Bandits.
quests.completion: Ten fewer knives in the dark. Take this: you have earned it.

quests.title: The Sunken Bastion
quests.text: The Sunken Bastion, a knight's hold that drowned in the fen a century ago, is where Voss's chart points. The old warden rolls say it once kept a Hearthpin safe, and the bells everyone keeps hearing ring from inside it. The cult has warded its door with grave-stones. Bring me one of the ward stones, {playerName}, and I will unweave the seal.
quests.completion: The ward parts like rotten rope. Ivara sent word that the Hearthpin fragment went warm at the very hour you brought me this stone. Whatever the Bastion keeps, the fragment knows it is there. The door stands open, and the dark below it is listening.

quests.title: Bristly Boar Hides
quests.text: Boar hide makes the finest travel packs, and the meadows northwest of town are crawling with the beasts. Bring me 5 Bristly Boar Hides and I will make it worth your time.
quests.completion: Ah, fine bristly hides! These will fetch a good price.

quests.title: Breaking the Seal
quests.text: The seal on the Sanctum was wrought with mountain-fire, and only mountain-fire will let us pass without tearing it wide open. The stormcrag elementals carry embers of that first forging in their cores. Bring me five Blessed Embers, {playerName}, for if the cult opens that gate first, they will not be careful, and the Wyrm will not wake gently.
quests.completion: They burn blue and clean: the mountain remembers its old oath. With these I can unbind the gate for us alone.

quests.title: The Broodmother
quests.text: You have seen the webs, now ask yourself what spins cables thick as a man's wrist. The wardens call her the Broodmother, and her clutch hangs over Widow Thicket like a second canopy. Smash 8 of her eggs and put the old mother down before the rest can hatch. Mind the clutch, some eggs will not go quietly.
quests.completion: Dead? Truly dead? Then the thicket is just trees again. The Light bless your blade, {playerName}.

quests.title: Calming the Deep
quests.text: The sporelings of the Gleaming Deep were gentle folk before the tear touched their rings. What the corruption takes, it does not give back. Grant the corrupted ones rest, {playerName}: ten of them, in the north of the Deep.
quests.completion: You did what I could not bear to. The gatherers still sing in the south rings; because of you, they will keep singing.

quests.title: Break the War-Camp
quests.text: Drogmar's war-camp squats in the eastern crags, and his crushers are the spine of it, each one worth three of my soldiers. Take companions; this is no errand for one blade. Break ten crushers and the warlord's muster breaks with them.
quests.completion: Ten crushers down. The war-camp is a body without a spine. Time to take the head.

quests.title: Robes in the Reeds
quests.text: There, north past the third lake, where the mist never lifts. Grey robes, grey banners: Gravecallers, camped in the open like they already own the fen. This is no handful of fanatics, {playerName}. It is a cell of something larger, paid and supplied, and they have stopped hiding, which means they think they have already won. Prove them wrong. Cut down 12 of their cultists.
quests.completion: Twelve robes face-down in the mud. Every one carried the same pay, and not one would say whose. Now they know the fen watches back.

quests.title: Orders from Below
quests.text: The zealots move with purpose now, watches set and supplies counted, like soldiers before a siege. Cultists who organize are cultists taking orders, {playerName}. One of them is carrying written orders from below. Find the zealot who has them and bring the orders to me: I would know the hand that commands them.
quests.completion: This script... I last saw its like in Eastbrook. The same hand has guided every grave we have fought over, {playerName}.

quests.title: The Deacon of the Mire
quests.text: So a deacon of the Gravecallers stands at the heart of that camp, singing my drowned wardens up out of the lakes to serve him. Maren says he carries a chart he never lets out of his sight, and I want to know why. His hymn ends today. Take the camp road north, {playerName}, and put Deacon Voss in the ground, deep enough that nobody sings HIM back up.
quests.completion: Voss is dead, and in his coat was a chart of the Sunken Bastion, drawn by someone who has walked its drowned halls. The mist over the camp is already thinning. Now only the Bastion remains.

quests.title: The Deepfen Stirs
quests.text: The Deepfen mudfins kept to their shallows for twenty years. Now they swarm the east bank, dredging the lake bed day and night, and my wardens swear someone on the far shore pays them for what they haul up. I do not know who, and I do not like a marsh with a market in it. Cull 12 of the snappers and break their digging.
quests.completion: That will push them back to the mud for a while. But a mudfin does not dig for pay unless someone taught it what pay is. Somebody out there is buying, and I mean to learn what.

quests.title: Back to the Shallows
quests.text: Aldric says those idols are cult-make, which means the mudfins are hauling the marsh's old evil up one armful at a time, and it all funnels through their reed-huts on the shallows. I will not have it washing onto my causeway. Take this firebottle, get right up against each hut, and burn the lot. Five should break their dredging for good.
quests.completion: Ruthless and thorough. If this marsh ever dries out, there's warden's work waiting for you.

quests.title: The Dawnbound Tome
quests.text: The Light does not rest in you quietly, {playerName}. I have watched you lay the dead to peace, and I believe you are ready for what few paladins are ever taught: the Rite of Recall, by which a fallen soul is called back to the living. Its words are kept in the Dawnbound Tome, here in my keeping, but a book is no blessing while the restless dead still walk this ground. Return 6 more Restless Bones to the earth, and I will begin to teach you.
quests.completion: The chapel yard grows quiet. You are ready for the words, {playerName}, but the Rite of Recall cannot be spoken in a warm chapel. It must be sung where the veil between life and death wears thin. I mean to carry the Tome north into the Mirefen Marsh. Follow me there, and we will finish this.

quests.title: Ash on the Wind
quests.text: Look south off the palisade, {playerName}. Those fires in the dunes are not troll cookfires, they are ashbone musters, and every night there are more. The dead come up out of the bonefields with sand still in their teeth. Cut down ten raiders before they cut a road to my gate.
quests.completion: Ten fewer blades in the dunes, and the muster fires burned lower last night. My sentries slept, which they have not done in a week. Well cut, {playerName}.

quests.title: Banners over the Dunes
quests.text: The ashbone muster at the old bonefield graves, {playerName}, and my patrols cannot read the dunes the way they read a wall. Kill five of their warcallers, the ones that scream the dead upright, and plant a warning banner on each muster ground so my sentries can mark it from the ridge.
quests.completion: Three banners snapping in the hot wind, right where my glass can find them. With five warcallers silenced, whatever answers their call will come slower. You bought us time, {playerName}.

quests.title: Marrow and Ash
quests.text: Every ashbone raider carries a war-brand, {playerName}: a scorched tally of the host it marches under. I have counted four hosts from this ridge, but guesses are not intelligence. Bring me six brands off the raiders and their warcallers, and I will give Brannoc the shape of the war that is coming.
quests.completion: Six brands, and one mark burned into every one of them. This is no raid muster, {playerName}. Every host in the dunes answers to the wargate below us, the trolls call it Orkadia, and no five soldiers I ever served with could break what drums behind that door. Perhaps five like you.

quests.title: Matriarch of the Maw
quests.text: The scales told it true, {playerName}. I climbed the rim at dawn and saw her on the crater floor: Cindraleth, the matriarch every emberwing in this sky was hatched under, gold as a coal about to catch. While she broods, the drakes grow bolder, and Wyrmwatch cannot fight dragons and the ashbone both. End her in her crater, then carry the word to Gatecaptain Brannoc. Do not go alone.
quests.completion: The sky over the Drakemaw has been empty for two days, and now you walk through my gate with a matriarch's blood on your boots. Wyrmwatch has stood forty years on watch for exactly this, {playerName}. Take these pauldrons, mawscale, worked by our own smith. Wear them where the drakes can see.

quests.title: Scales of the Maw
quests.text: When the wind turns off the Drakemaw, the emberwing drakes ride it over my camp low enough to count their teeth, {playerName}. They range farther every day, and something in that crater drives them. Bring me three of their scales. Scales remember heat, and I can read where a drake has been roosting by the burn.
quests.completion: Look at the underside of this one, {playerName}: scorched in a spiral, and only one thing nests in circles. These drakes are brood-guards. Something in the Drakemaw is a mother.

quests.title: Scorched Stores
quests.text: The last wagon burned, {playerName}, but iron-strapped crates do not burn through. Four of them are still lying scorched along the dunes road with a season of salt, nails, and bowstrings inside. Bring my stores home before the trolls work out how to open them.
quests.completion: Scorched black and every latch still holding. The smith gets his nails, the fletcher her strings, and you get the boots I was saving for whoever brought my crates back, {playerName}.

quests.title: Trolls on the Road
quests.text: The dune trolls have learned the sound of a supply wagon, {playerName}. They hit the Cinder Dunes road three times this month, and the last driver walked in carrying nothing but the reins. Eight trolls off that road and my wagons roll again.
quests.completion: Eight, and my drivers have stopped writing farewell letters before every run. The garrison eats because of you, {playerName}.

quests.title: The Watcher at the Wargate
quests.text: Something is pulling the ashbone east, {playerName}, and I sent my best to learn what. Scout Yerrin has camped a month in the far dunes past Trollmoot, in sight of a gate nobody built in my lifetime. Her reports stopped ten days ago. Find her camp and get me her eyes.
quests.completion: Brannoc sent you? Then my last runner never made it. Keep your voice down and sit, {playerName}. You see that gate below? Count the war-banners in front of it, and you will understand why I stopped writing things down.

quests.title: Warlord Drogmar
quests.text: Warlord Drogmar took the Broodsworn's coin and swore the clans to the mountain's waking. He is the hammer they mean to swing at my wall, and when he slams the ground, {playerName}, do not be standing near him. Take your companions into the war-camp and end him, for Highwatch.
quests.completion: Drogmar, dead in his own camp. The clans will scatter to the high passes: you have bought my wall a winter, {playerName}.

quests.title: The Drowned Dead
quests.text: The dead walking out of the lakes are sailors, {playerName}. I know the cut of their coats: the crews of the ships that went missing off the harbor these past years, still hung with the weeds they died in. The sea took them, and something brought them here to stand guard in the fog. Return 12 of the Drowned Dead to their rest.
quests.completion: Each one you fell is a sailor set free. Some of them still carried Eastbrook harbor tokens in their pockets. Whoever drowned them is filling this fen like a tithing box, and the box is not yet full.

quests.title: Censers from the Deep
quests.text: North of the widow lake stands a chapel that drowned with its congregation when the marsh rose. The dead there carry rusted censers, funerary ones, the kind swung at a Gravecaller rite. Gather 4 from the chapel yard and I will read what rite was sung over that water.
quests.completion: As I feared. These censers burned grave-ash, not incense. Someone consecrated that chapel to the drowning, and the rite is signed 'Voss.'

quests.title: The Drowned Choir
quests.text: The waders do not act alone. Among them walk the Drowned Votaries, the cult that sank with the temple, still in their rotted vestments, still singing the prayer from the shore-rocks. Silence eight of them, and bring me six of the offerings they carry. I would know what they mean to give their goddess.
quests.completion: Pearls, knuckle-bones, a child's carved fish... grave-gifts, {playerName}. They are not raising the dead. They are dressing them, the way you dress a body for burial. The temple is a tomb that refuses to close.

quests.title: The Drowned Moon
quests.text: I have read the last of the rubbings, {playerName}, and I understand now what the cult drowned themselves to keep asleep. Ysolei, the Drowned Moon made flesh, coils on the altar at the temple's heart, and the stolen warmth of every life the mere took is pouring into her waking. When the moon stands full she rises, and the water rises with her: the tarn, the wall, the whole mountain under it. Gather the strongest you can find and put her back to sleep. For good, this time.
quests.completion: The altar is dark, the water is still, and the moon over the tarn is only the moon. You drowned a goddess tonight, {playerName}, and the mountain will never know how close it came. Let the wardens of the shore-rocks rest easy at last.

objectives.label: Ysolei, Avatar of the Drowned Moon, slain

quests.title: Clippings from the Living Green
quests.text: You want to understand this garden? Then read it the way I do. The stags that graze the lawns grow the truest green: every leaf on them is a page. Bring me six fresh clippings from the topiary stags, {playerName}. They will not thank you for the pruning, but they will regrow. Everything here regrows.
quests.completion: Look here: the leaves are curling in on themselves, every clipping the same. The garden is afraid, {playerName}. In a hundred years I have never once known it afraid.

quests.title: The Bull of the Fountain Court
quests.text: Now the truth, {playerName}. The bull at the heart of the maze was my masterwork: I shaped him to guard the Fountain Court, and for a hundred years he did. But the fear in the green has reached him, and he guards nothing now, he hunts. The maze feeds him whoever wanders in. I am too old to unmake him, and it must be unmaking, root and branch. Bring a friend, walk the maze to the court, and cut my bull down.
quests.completion: I felt it, here, when he came apart. A hundred years of work, and you were right to end it. Take this mantle: I cut it for whoever proved stronger than my best. The court is only a fountain tonight, {playerName}, and the garden is only a garden. Perhaps now the Head Gardener and I can both sleep.

quests.title: The Four Quiet Sisters
quests.text: When the garden was young, the first gardeners raised four marble sisters to watch its quarters: one above the Rose Wilds, one on the pond walk east of the maze, one on the west lawn where the gnomes keep their warren, and one on the south lawn past the hedges. The maze grew up between them, and most folk never see all four. Walk the quarters, {playerName}, and press your palm to each sister. When the garden has looked you over from all four sides, it will open places it keeps from strangers.
quests.completion: Four rubbings, four sisters, and not one of them wept marble. The garden has taken your measure, {playerName}, and it did not find you wanting. Now I can send you where the trouble truly lives.

quests.title: Word Through the Gate
quests.text: The lawns past this gate have trimmed themselves for a hundred years, {playerName}, and lately they have started trimming visitors. Head Gardener Amaranth keeps the books in Hedgewick, up the road past the gate lawns. Tell her another traveler has come through, and tell her the hedges by the gate moved last night.
quests.completion: Moved, did they. Pell reports that every week, and every week he is right. Forgive my eyes, {playerName}, I have not slept a whole night in years: someone has to watch the garden watch us. Welcome to Hedgewick.

quests.title: The Groundskeepers Grudge
quests.text: The shears were only the start, {playerName}. Last night the gnomes tipped our tool carts into the green, one out by their warren west of the maze, one clean across the garden on the pond walk, and scattered a hundred years of good iron in the grass. Drive off eight of the little devils and haul the spilled carts home.
quests.completion: Three carts back and the pegs full again. Let the little devils sulk in their hedges: Hedgewick works these lawns too.

quests.title: Pruned into Hunger
quests.text: Whoever shapes this garden has grown careless, or cruel. The wolf shapes out in the Rose Wilds were clipped for show, yet lately they hunt: green jaws, no bellies, and no reason ever to stop. Cut down ten topiary wolves, {playerName}, and let the lawns be lawns again for a while.
quests.completion: Ten heaps of clippings where ten wolves stood. It should feel like gardening, {playerName}. Why does it feel like war?

quests.title: The Stolen Shears
quests.text: Every pair of shears in Hedgewick has walked off in a fortnight, {playerName}: off the pegs, out of locked sheds, one pair out of my own apron while I dozed. It is the hedge gnomes, the little groundskeepers who hate us walking their lawns. Get six pairs back before the whole hamlet is down to kitchen knives.
quests.completion: Six pairs, and my own among them, I would know the nick in the blade anywhere. Here, these gloves were knitted for pruning work. Warm hands make steady shears.

quests.title: Who Trims the Hedges
quests.text: I have kept the ledgers thirty years, {playerName}, and not slept properly for ten of them, because the sums will not close. Grass wants cutting and hedges want shaping, and nobody here does either, yet every dawn the garden stands trimmed. Lately the woodfolk swear they see an old man with a barrow on the far south lawns, past the maze by the Lily Basin. Find him. If he is real, I can finally sleep. If he is not, I suppose I never will.
quests.completion: So the house finally sent someone. A hundred years I have walked these lawns, {playerName}, and the garden and I have an understanding: I trim what asks to be trimmed. Sit. The hedges can spare you an hour.

objectives.label: Find the gardener by the Lily Basin

quests.title: The Mountain Wakes
quests.text: Stormcrag has stood silent a thousand years, and now the very stones of it get up and walk. Elementals do not simply wake, {playerName}. Something beneath this mountain is turning in its sleep. Put twelve of them down so I may study what remains.
quests.completion: The fragments hum like struck bells. The mountain is not angry, {playerName}... it is being disturbed.

quests.title: First Furrow
quests.text: Take this hoe and a pinch of vale wheat seed, {playerName}. Sow the seed in one of the beds beside me, then go about your business. Come back whenever you like and bring the crop in; I will be here.
quests.completion: There, your first crop in your own hands. It keeps growing while you are away, and it never spoils. Your Harvest Journal (Shift+K, or the Farming row of your Professions window) lists every planted bed and its timer. Come back for seed whenever the beds call you, {playerName}.

quests.title: The Lost Caravan
